name: manual_559e29
claim: Before global heartbeat cleanup, stop affected workers, automatic restarts and queue mutations, and keep them quiesced until cleanup finishes; recheck the complete affected set under that maintenance window. If continuing quiescence cannot be established, do not run cleanup: the current implementation does not atomically recheck liveness before releasing each claim, so a restarting worker can lose its claim. Heartbeat cleanup now handles both legacy and queue claims for all agents classified DEAD, so verify liveness and independently inspect every affected claim before operator-authorized global cleanup; stale heartbeat alone does not prove death. Cleanup requeues queue claims even at the retry limit: hold exhausted or unsafe work and seek separately reviewed authorized recovery. An agent release event alone does not clear a queue claim. Queue completion requires queue complete <task_id> <claimant_id> --expected-claimed-at <claimed_at> and checks both the current claimant and that claim's timestamp; never impersonate an absent claimant. Verify completion artifacts independently, and remember a reserved handoff retains required_agent_id after requeue. Pass the claimed_at printed by your own queue claim. --unverified-legacy skips that fence: use it when your own stamp is lost, or in a takeover disclosed under the author-actor takeover policy.

decisions.notes: Corrects the command form in lesson_3b5f83545a8e: since PR 525, queue complete and queue fail require --expected-claimed-at or --unverified-legacy, so the old command form is rejected. Older worktrees that share the queue database can still finish a task without a fence; the operator ruled this grandfathered by design on 2026-11-27.
